questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Social life, courses, language

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The University of Edinburgh does a good job providing you information and replying to your messages if you have any questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did receive assistance through email because you are inked up with a student adviser, that replies very quickly and guides you through the most important things.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is super easy to apply through University of Edinburgh for one of their student accommodations. It def the easier and some cheaper option

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
That you still live extremely close to campus and in the middle of the city. 
You pay less for a good location because the rooms are in worse condition. The further away from the center and campus you get the better condition of the rooms but the higher the price. I choose location > condition of the room and I would 100% do it again. Good location is key.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is a little bit hard to see what to expect for the different accommodations but it was my impression that most of the ones in the city center looked kinda the same.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You apply through the website of University of Edinburgh as any other normal student and this website will take you through the necessary steps.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was no like service or mail to text (as I remember) but the sit was very user-friendly and straight forward

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do it in advance (like in good time)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's different from UCPH but it was still fun

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: 1.-2. year courses are a lot easier than the 3.-4. year courses. The difference is very big and the type of exams are very different. Because I was on my master the 3.-4. year courses were def the most challenging but still at a reasonable level

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: They consist of lectures (forelæsninger), seminars (seminar) and tutorials. Seminar and lectures are known at UCPH whereas tutorials consists of a group of 10 people doing exercises with an older student often a PhD student. My favourite was the tutorials, you learned a lot there

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Critical Legal Thinking, International Private Law, WTO Law and Mental Health Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: International Private Law because it was super interesting and the exam very familiar with exams from UCPH. Mental Health Law because the teacher was very engaged in the students and their understanding of the subject and the exam was an essay written over 4 weeks so super manageable.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I traveled more than I expected so that was a cost I did not calculate

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Buying groceries and bus is super cheap. Trains to other parts of scotland can be super cheap if you find a good deal. Scotrail (the train company of scotland) often have 50% on tickets for students so keep an eye out on their website.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is a lot a lot of sports clubs and other clubs to join!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of societies that was about culture, not only the scottish one but also other countries in the world. There were a very high number of sport clubs/societies to join and also some social societies. I would recommend checking out their website.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: going to stramash on Wednesdays. They host a free ceilidh evening where you can learn to dance ceilidh and its very fun

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the rest of the country! Aberdeen, Glasgow, Inverness, Loch Ness, Glennfinnan Viaduct, Isle of Skye, Isle of Arran, Isle of Murray. Going hiking in the nearby areas or even in edinburgh itself. Seeing all the castles and the cliffs in scotland.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Scottish culture is not too different from danish so you get used to it by like a month.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be very open. You are the one that has to approach them since they can be a bit reserved but scottish people are super nice

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: did not find anything challenging

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: their politeness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) choose courses out of interest
2) choose a good location for your accommodation
3) be as open as possible towards everyone in the first weeks to create a social group of friends
4) still be open later on to new friendships!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I can't think of anything

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: the friends I got and the way of teaching the tutorials opened my eyes for how useful they can be.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: saying goodbye to my friends

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: nope

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
